$schema: Each key is an event id from docs/design/events.md (plus quiet_day, illness.<condition-id>, and derelict_* outcome variants). Value: array of text variants. Placeholders: {name} crew member, {n} number, {item} supply name.
quiet_day: Nothing happened today. The crew found this suspicious.
The stars held still. So did everything else.
A quiet day. Somebody wrote it down in case it never happens again.
The drives hummed. Nobody complained, which was a first.
The crew played cards for rations they already owned.
Dull day aboard. The ship's cat, if there is one, was not consulted.
The coffee was bad in the usual way. Morale held.
Hours of empty space went by, as scheduled.
Someone counted the rations twice. The number did not improve.
The hull ticked and creaked, then thought better of it.
A buoy blinked in the distance and was not heard from again.
The crew debated whether it was Tuesday. It was not settled.
The ship's clock lost four minutes. It was returned.
The view was stars. They were the same stars as yesterday, mostly.
Somebody hummed a hymn through the whole afternoon shift.
The recycler gurgled once, with feeling, and went quiet.
The crew mended socks. In space this counts as a hobby.
Not a single alarm sounded. The captain checked the alarms.
The Lane stayed where it was. A small mercy.
A dull glow on the horizon turned out to be a dull glow.
Everyone agreed the day was fine. Nobody trusted it.
The ship drifted through nothing at a respectable pace.
A long, level watch. The log entry is one word: fine.
The captain read the manual again. It was no more helpful.
illness: {name} is not feeling well. The medical locker has opinions.
{name} took to a bunk with a look nobody liked.
{name} has come down with something. The manual calls it a condition.
illness.space-dysentery: {name} has caught space dysentery. The recycler is being blamed.
{name} has space dysentery. The bunks nearest the head have been reassigned.
{name} has space dysentery. Nobody is sure how, and nobody asked.
illness.hull-mold-fever: {name} has hull mold fever. The walls look smug about it.
{name} has hull mold fever. The mold has been asked to leave.
{name} has come down with hull mold fever and a green cough.
illness.cryo-fever: {name} has cryo-fever. They are cold, then colder, then confusing.
{name} has caught cryo-fever. Blankets have been requisitioned.
{name} has cryo-fever. The thermostat is innocent, officially.
illness.scurvy: {name} has scurvy. It is 2184 and the gums have not heard.
{name} has scurvy. The crew suggests fruit, of which there is none.
illness.radiation-sickness: {name} has radiation sickness. The suit was, regrettably, in the locker.
{name} has radiation sickness and a mild glow. This is not a joke.
{name} has radiation sickness. The manual said this would not happen.
illness.exhaustion: {name} is exhausted. The drives have been running longer than anyone.
{name} has fallen asleep on watch, upright. The crew is worn thin.
The crew is exhausted, {name} most of all. The ship, strangely, is not.
illness.decompression-injury: {name} has a decompression injury. It is mostly the bruise that talks.
{name} came through the crossing with a decompression injury and a story.
{name} has a decompression injury. They will tell it at every station.
illness.micrometeorite-puncture: {name} was punctured by a micrometeorite. The suit would have helped, had it been worn.
A micrometeorite pierced {name}. It was very small and very sure of itself.
{name} has a micrometeorite puncture. The pebble has not been found.
pirates: Pirates boarded while you slept. They took {n} {item} and left a note complimenting the coffee.
Pirates took {n} {item} and apologized for the inconvenience. The apology was on a form.
Raiders came aboard politely and left with {n} {item}. They signed the manifest.
Pirates relieved you of {n} {item}. They said it was nothing personal.
lost_lane: You lost the Lane. It took {n} days to find a buoy that would admit to being one.
The buoys went quiet and the ship went sideways. You lost {n} days finding the Lane.
You drifted off the Lane. The cost was {n} days and some dignity.
drive_failure: An ion drive has died. It made a small sound and then no more sound.
An ion drive has failed for good. The crew stood about with hats off, metaphorically.
One of your drives has given up. It had a long run and a bad attitude.
drive_stall: An ion drive has stalled. It needs {n} days of rest and a stern word.
A drive went offline for {n} days. Coaxing was attempted and ignored.
A drive sulked and shut itself down for {n} days. Nobody asked it why.
hull_puncture: A hull plate has cracked. The crew applied tape, which is not in the manual.
The hull took a hit and a plate gave out. It is, strictly, a leak.
A hull plate has broken. You can hear the cold from the corridor.
pump_failure: The coolant pump has failed. The ship will not move until it is mended.
The coolant pump coughed twice and stopped. The drives are waiting, politely.
The pump is broken. Everything else is fine, which is no help.
gyro_failure: The nav gyro has failed. North is now a matter of opinion.
The nav gyro is broken. It has been pointing at nothing for an hour.
The gyro gave out. The crew navigates by feel, and feel is not good.
hull_fire: A fire in the galley burned {n} rations. {name} was scorched putting it out.
Fire broke out aft. It cost {n} rations, and {name} came out singed.
A small fire became a large one. {n} rations burned, and {name} is sore.
crew_eva_drift: {name} went out on a spacewalk and drifted off. They should be back in {n} days.
{name} is adrift on a tether that is no longer tethered. Expect {n} days.
{name} stepped outside for air, of which there is none. Back in {n} days.
bad_recycler: The water recycler has gone bad. The crew drank before anyone noticed.
The recycler is running brown. Everyone is a little worse for it.
Bad water. The recycler is sorry, and so is everyone who drank it.
derelict: You came upon a derelict. It was empty, and it was clearly there first.
A dark hull drifted past. The crew searched it and found only dust and a calendar.
A wreck hung off the starboard side. It was already picked clean, by the look.
derelict_nothing: You searched a derelict and found nothing but a calendar from 2149.
The derelict had been picked clean. Someone had left a polite note saying so.
derelict_rations: You found a derelict with {n} rations still in the locker. Nobody asked who the previous owner was.
The wreck held {n} rations, mostly sealed. You took them without a speech.
derelict_part: A derelict gave up a spare: one {item}, in good order. The ship was grateful.
You salvaged a spare {item} from a drifting hulk. It was warm and strangely welcome.
derelict_suits: A derelict held {n} EVA suits, used but sealed. The crew is better dressed.
You found {n} suits in a wreck. They smell of someone else, which is acceptable.
algae_bloom: An algae bloom in the tank yielded {n} rations. It tastes like pond, but it is food.
The hydroponics bay bloomed overnight. You gained {n} rations and a green smell.
A wild algae bloom turned up in the tanks. {n} rations were harvested, thankfully.
belter_help: A passing Belter pointed to a cache and left. You gained {n} rations and thanked the dark.
Belters shared {n} rations and no conversation. It was a good trade.
A Belter tossed over {n} rations and a grunt. The grunt was friendly.
cargo_shift: The cargo shifted coming out of the crossing. {n} {item} went missing in the hold.
Loose lashing. You lost {n} {item} to the crossing and a bad knot.
The crossing shook the hold, and {n} {item} did not survive the shaking.
